Mouldy
mōl'dē
adj. (overgrown with mould; the state of the bread by which the Gibeonites deceived Joshua)
From mould, a growth on decaying matter, Middle English mowlde. The Hebrew niqqud here means crumbly or spotted — bread deliberately aged to tell a lie about distance.

Biblical Definition

Both occurrences are in one deception. The Gibeonites, hearing what had happened to Jericho and Ai, dressed a delegation to look as though it had come a very long way: “And old shoes and clouted upon their feet, and old garments upon them; and all the bread of their provision was dry and mouldy” (Jos 9:5). Then they said it in words: “This our bread we took hot for our provision out of our houses on the day we came forth to go unto you; but now, behold, it is dry, and it is mouldy” (Jos 9:12). The evidence was manufactured, and it worked, because Israel examined the evidence instead of asking God: the men took of their victuals and asked not counsel at the mouth of the LORD. “And Joshua made peace with them, and made a league with them, to let them live: and the princes of the congregation sware unto them” (Jos 9:15). Three days later the truth came out — “they heard that they were their neighbours, and that they dwelt among them” (Jos 9:16) — and the oath still stood. Israel kept it, and four centuries later God avenged Saul's breach of it.

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines mouldy as overgrown with mould; covered or filled with the minute fungous growth that appears on damp or decaying substances.

expand to see more

MOULD, n. Concreted matter; a substance like down which forms on bodies which lie long in warm and damp air.

MOULDY, a. Overgrown with mould.

All the bread of their provision was dry and mouldy. Josh. ix.

MOULDINESS, n. The state of being mouldy.

Key Scripture

Jos 9:5 — "And old shoes and clouted upon their feet, and old garments upon them; and all the bread of their provision was dry and mouldy."

Jos 9:12 — "This our bread we took hot for our provision out of our houses on the day we came forth to go unto you; but now, behold, it is dry, and it is mouldy:"

Jos 9:15 — "And Joshua made peace with them, and made a league with them, to let them live: and the princes of the congregation sware unto them."

Jos 9:16 — "And it came to pass at the end of three days after they had made a league with them, that they heard that they were their neighbours, and that they dwelt among them."

Modern Corruption

Joshua 9 is the standing warning that examined evidence is not the same as sought counsel, and it is the step the chapter says Israel skipped.

expand to see more

Israel did not act carelessly by modern standards. They questioned the delegation, they inspected the provisions, they handled the cracked wineskins and the mouldy bread, and the physical evidence supported the story in every particular. The chapter's verdict on all this diligence is one clause: they asked not counsel at the mouth of the LORD. That is the sentence to hang over every decision made by good process. Evidence can be manufactured; a document can be produced; references can be arranged; and a man who has checked everything checkable may still have consulted no one who knows what he cannot see. Prayer in Scripture is not a devotional garnish on a decision otherwise well made. It is the step by which a people who cannot see the heart ask the One who can.

The second half of the chapter is harder and more instructive. When the deception came out three days later, the congregation murmured against the princes and wanted the Gibeonites destroyed. The princes refused, on one ground: we have sworn unto them by the LORD God of Israel; now therefore we may not touch them. The oath had been obtained by fraud, and it still bound, because the name sworn by was God's and the honour at stake was His. Israel kept it. Centuries afterwards Saul, in his zeal, broke it and slew Gibeonites, and God sent a three-year famine in David's reign on that account. So the chapter that begins with a bad decision ends by teaching how a bad decision is to be handled: not by pretending it did not happen, and not by adding a broken word to a foolish one, but by keeping faith and bearing the cost.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew niqqud (H5350), crumbs or mouldy bread; with yabesh (H3001), dry, and shaba (H7650), to swear — the oath that outlived the fraud.

expand to see more

Hebrew niqqud (H5350) — crumbled, mouldy bread; used only in Joshua 9 and in a gift of cracknels; Joshua 9:5, 1 Kings 14:3.

Hebrew yabesh (H3001) — dry, withered; the bread was dry and mouldy; Joshua 9:12.

Hebrew shaba (H7650) — to swear; the princes of the congregation sware unto them; Joshua 9:15.

Hebrew shaal (H7592) — to ask, to enquire; they asked not counsel at the mouth of the LORD; Joshua 9:14.

Hebrew berith (H1285) — a covenant, a league; made in error and kept for centuries; Joshua 9:15.

Usage

"“All the bread of their provision was dry and mouldy” — evidence manufactured for a lie."

"“The princes of the congregation sware unto them” — and the oath outlived the fraud."

"“They heard that they were their neighbours” — three days too late, and the word still held."
